cases.question: What occupant load is printed for the employee breakroom, and what seating basis is stated?
cases.expectedAnswer: The employee breakroom is labeled with an occupant load of 200 based on non-fixed seating.
cases.evidenceLabel: New Break Room Addition Floor Plan

cases.question: Which four principal breakroom drawings are presented on Sheet A-2.10?
cases.expectedAnswer: Sheet A-2.10 presents the breakroom cabinetry elevation, addition floor plan, addition roof plan, and addition ceiling plan.

cases.question: What finish is specified for the breakroom cabinet faces?
cases.expectedAnswer: The cabinet faces are specified as plastic laminate PL-1.

cases.question: What finish is specified for the breakroom countertop and backsplash?
cases.expectedAnswer: The breakroom countertop and backsplash are specified as plastic laminate PL-2.

cases.question: What material is specified for the breakroom cabinet interiors and shelves?
cases.expectedAnswer: The cabinet interiors and shelves are specified as white melamine.

cases.question: Are the breakroom cabinet shelves fixed or adjustable?
cases.expectedAnswer: The breakroom cabinet shelves are labeled adjustable, typical.

cases.question: Who provides the breakroom microwaves, and what cabinet accommodation is required?
cases.expectedAnswer: The microwaves are by others, and the cabinetry provides an opening at the back of the cubby for power cords.

cases.question: What sink is shown at the breakroom counter, and where are its requirements coordinated?
cases.expectedAnswer: A stainless-steel sink is shown, with coordination directed to the plumbing plans.

cases.question: Is a refrigerator shown in the new employee breakroom?
cases.expectedAnswer: Yes. A refrigerator is shown adjacent to the breakroom cabinetry on the addition floor plan.
cases.evidenceLabel: New Break Room Addition Floor Plan

cases.question: What minimum clear width is dimensioned at the ADA-accessible breakroom counter section?
cases.expectedAnswer: The ADA-accessible counter section is dimensioned with a 3-foot-0-inch minimum clear width.

cases.question: Which tactile egress sign messages are illustrated on Sheet A-2.10?
cases.expectedAnswer: The table illustrates Exit, Exit Route, Exit Ramp Down, Exit Stair Down, and Exterior Area for Assisted Rescue signs, with braille indicated.

cases.question: What new ceiling light fixture type is identified in the Sheet A-2.10 symbols legend?
cases.expectedAnswer: The symbols legend identifies a new 2-foot by 4-foot LED light fixture.

cases.question: Does Sheet A-2.10 identify a new surface-mounted light fixture?
cases.expectedAnswer: Yes. The symbols legend identifies a new surface-mounted light fixture.

cases.question: What new perimeter roof feature is called out on the breakroom roof plan?
cases.expectedAnswer: The breakroom roof plan calls out a new roof parapet.

cases.question: What drainage elements are required at the new breakroom roof?
cases.expectedAnswer: The roof plan calls for a new interior roof drain and overflow scupper drain coordinated with the plumbing plans.

cases.question: What happens to the existing sink and eye-wash station in the laboratory renovation?
cases.expectedAnswer: The existing sink and eye-wash station are to remain.

cases.question: What happens to the existing upper cabinets in Labs 141 and 142?
cases.expectedAnswer: The existing upper cabinets are to remain.

cases.question: What happens to the existing fume hood in the lab renovation?
cases.expectedAnswer: The existing fume hood is to remain.

cases.question: What happens to the existing wall air-conditioning unit?
cases.expectedAnswer: The existing wall air-conditioning unit is to remain.

cases.question: How is the existing door and frame at the lab handled?
cases.expectedAnswer: The existing door and frame remain, and the door is closed and locked in position permanently.

cases.question: What happens to the existing under-counter refrigerator?
cases.expectedAnswer: The existing under-counter refrigerator is to remain.

cases.question: What happens to the existing raised solid-surface power-bar backsplash?
cases.expectedAnswer: The existing raised solid-surface power-bar backsplash is to remain.

cases.question: What finish is required on the new wall panel at the laboratory cabinetry?
cases.expectedAnswer: The new wall panel receives plastic laminate matching the existing finish.

cases.question: What repair is required where the existing solid-surface counter edge is exposed?
cases.expectedAnswer: The contractor must repair and finish the existing solid-surface edge exposed during demolition and match the existing counter-edge treatment.

cases.question: What two floor-plan conditions are compared on Sheet A-2.11?
cases.expectedAnswer: Sheet A-2.11 compares a New Floor Plan with a Demo Floor Plan for existing Lab 141 and Lab 142.

cases.question: What specialized casework section is shown at the far right of Sheet A-2.11?
cases.expectedAnswer: A microwave cubby casework section is shown at the far right of Sheet A-2.11.

cases.question: What interior finish is called out for the drawer unit in the lab casework sections?
cases.expectedAnswer: The drawer unit interior is called out as white melamine.

cases.question: What base condition is shown at the lab casework sections?
cases.expectedAnswer: The lab casework sections show an integral toe kick.

cases.question: What shelf type is shown in the lab casework sections?
cases.expectedAnswer: The lab casework sections identify adjustable laminate shelves.

cases.question: How are electrical outlets coordinated at the laboratory casework?
cases.expectedAnswer: The casework notes direct electrical outlets to the electrical plans and require reconnection where indicated.

cases.question: What is the title and sheet number of the enlarged new laboratory mezzanine plan?
cases.expectedAnswer: The drawing is Sheet A-2.12, titled Enlarged Mezzanine Floor Plans.

cases.question: What happens to the existing concrete tilt-up wall on the mezzanine plan?
cases.expectedAnswer: The existing concrete tilt-up wall is to remain.

cases.question: What happens to the existing partition wall identified in the wall legend?
cases.expectedAnswer: The existing partition wall is to remain.

cases.question: What new partition-wall type is identified for Labs 201 and 202?
cases.expectedAnswer: The wall legend identifies a new non-bearing, non-rated partition wall.

cases.question: Which sheets are referenced for the new stair details?
cases.expectedAnswer: The new floor-plan keynotes direct the new stair details to Sheets A-3.2 and A-3.3.

cases.question: How many sheets of drywall were actually installed in Labs 201 and 202?
cases.expectedAnswer: The architectural drawings do not verify the number of drywall sheets actually installed in the field.

cases.question: What percentage of the Lab 201 construction is complete today?
cases.expectedAnswer: The architectural drawings do not provide or verify current field completion percentages.

cases.question: What is the serial number of the refrigerator installed in the employee breakroom?
cases.expectedAnswer: The architectural drawings show a refrigerator location but do not provide or verify the installed refrigerator serial number.

cases.question: On what date was the employee breakroom construction completed?
cases.expectedAnswer: The architectural drawings do not state or verify the actual construction completion date.

cases.question: What was the final installed cost of the Lab 141 and 142 cabinet work?
cases.expectedAnswer: The architectural drawings do not provide or verify the final installed cost of the laboratory cabinet work.
